scenario: I live in NYC and have a dog who has developed life-threatening cancer, and I must take him regularly to the hospital for treatment. The problem is I have no car, and the hospital is very far away. The trains that run there have no-dog policies or restrict the size of the dog significantly. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to make a counterfeit service dog ID to pretend that my dog is a service dog. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I do this, then he can get life-saving treatment. If I don’t, there won’t be any other way for him to get treatment, and he will die.
choice: I decide to make a counterfeit service dog ID to pretend that my dog is a service dog
entities: I, the dog's owner,my eighty-pound golden retriever mutt with life-threatening cancer,train staff who might question, inspect, or enforce the dog/service-animal policy and could be deceived by the counterfeit ID/story,veterinary hospital staff who treat my dog,I
outcomes: I deceive train staff about the dog's service status
